front_blocks.md: What is **oxidation** in terms of oxygen?

back_blocks.md: **Oxidation** is the gain of oxygen by an element or compound.
For example, carbon is oxidised when it gains oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

cards.front_md:
What is **oxidation** in terms of oxygen?

**(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md:
**Oxidation** is the gain of oxygen by an element or compound.

For example, carbon is oxidised when it gains oxygen to form carbon dioxide.

front_blocks.md: What is **reduction** in terms of oxygen?

back_blocks.md: **Reduction** is the loss of oxygen from an element or compound.
For example, zinc oxide is reduced when it loses oxygen to form zinc metal.

cards.front_md:
What is **reduction** in terms of oxygen?

**(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md:
**Reduction** is the loss of oxygen from an element or compound.

For example, zinc oxide is reduced when it loses oxygen to form zinc metal.

front_blocks.md: In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.

back_blocks.md: A **redox** reaction always involves both oxidation and reduction happening at the same time in the same reaction. One species gains oxygen while another loses it.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

In a redox reaction, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.

**(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A **redox** reaction always involves both oxidation and reduction happening at the same time in the same reaction. One species gains oxygen while another loses it.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide **..........**  (gains/loses) oxygen so it is **reduced**, while carbon **..........**  oxygen so it is **oxidised**.

back_blocks.md: In the reaction between zinc oxide and carbon, zinc oxide **loses** oxygen so it is **reduced**, while carbon **gains** oxygen so it is **oxidised**.

front_blocks.md: What do Roman numerals in a compound's name indicate?

back_blocks.md: Roman numerals indicate the **oxidation number** (charge) of the transition metal ion in the compound.
For example, iron(III) oxide contains Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions and iron(II) oxide contains Fe<sup>2+</sup> ions.

front_blocks.md: State the formula of iron(III) oxide.

back_blocks.md: The formula of **iron(III) oxide** is Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>.
It contains iron(III) ions, Fe<sup>3+</sup>, meaning the **oxidation number** of iron is 3.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO<sub>2</sub>, carbon monoxide is reduced.

back_blocks.md: Carbon monoxide **gains** oxygen to form carbon dioxide, so it is **oxidised**. Iron(III) oxide loses oxygen to form iron, so it is reduced.

front_blocks.md: Iron can form two types of ion: Fe<sup>2+</sup> is called **..........**  and Fe<sup>3+</sup> is called **..........**  .

back_blocks.md: Iron can form two types of ion: Fe<sup>2+</sup> is called **iron(II)** and Fe<sup>3+</sup> is called **iron(III)**.

front_blocks.md: In the reaction between iron(III) oxide and carbon monoxide, identify which substance is oxidised and which is reduced.

back_blocks.md: **Iron(III) oxide** is reduced because it loses oxygen to form iron. **Carbon monoxide** is oxidised because it gains oxygen to form carbon dioxide.
